action_items: Minor cleanup done by testing agent: removed two references to the undefined setter `setRespQuery` in /app/frontend/src/pages/EventPipeline.jsx (lines ~182 and ~478). These were leftovers from a prior refactor (the Responsabile search state now lives inside StaffAssignSelect's internal `q`). The references caused a Runtime error ('setRespQuery is not defined') the moment the task-edit Dialog's onOpenChange fired (e.g., when focus moved to the StaffAssignSelect popover for Aggiungi nuovo Staff). Main agent: please review the fix and keep the single state ownership inside StaffAssignSelect.
critical_code_review_comments: EventPipeline.jsx had a stale reference `setRespQuery` with no corresponding useState. It was never caught because the Dialog's onOpenChange handler is only invoked on explicit open-state changes; the first user interaction that triggered it blew up the whole page. Recommend adding a linter rule or quick smoke-test for the task-edit dialog save/close path.

StaffAssignSelect.jsx: '+ Aggiungi nuovo Staff' lives in a separate footer section under the staff list — DOM-wise this is already 'last' in reading order and under the search results, matching the spec. No change needed.

TeamMembersDialog.jsx candidates sort uses `label.localeCompare` where label = `${nome} ${cognome}` (pname). For the current fixtures this gives Davide Mora, Giulia Viola which looks OK, but if you want the same Cognome→Nome order used in StaffAssignSelect, consider sorting by `${cognome} ${nome}` for consistency. Not a spec blocker.
